deities: Sri Subrahmanyeswara Swamy with Srivalli and Devasena
festivals: Maha Sivaratri Brahmotsavams (Magha, February-March; includes Prabhotsavam, Gramotsavam, Kalyanotsavam and Dhwajarohana, during which childless devotees try to catch tossed Nandi Muddalu rice balls for blessings)
Prabha Mahotsavam (decorated chariots pulled through village streets)
Masa Sivaratri (monthly, with special rituals and Annadanam)
Kartheeka Masotsavams (month of lamps; Kumbhabhishekam on Arudra Nakshatram)
Sravana Masotsavams (August-September, with special pujas to Goddess Parvati)
Dasara/Navaratri (nine days with Navadurga alankarams and vahana sevas)

history.dynasty: Kakatiya, Chalukya, Reddy Kings, Vijayanagara Empire
history.period: Ancient; documented royal patronage from the Kakatiya, Chalukya, Reddy and Vijayanagara periods; renovated and consecrated in 1983
history.summary: The Sri Ramalingeswara Swamy Vari Devasthanam stands on a 612-foot hill at Yanamalakuduru in the southeast of Vijayawada, overlooking the River Krishna and the city. The main deity is a self-manifested (Swayambhu) Vayu-Linga placed on an eight-faced pedestal (Ashta Mukha Panapattam), so positioned that the sun's rays fall directly on it at sunrise. Tradition holds that Sage Parasurama consecrated the linga during his expiatory journey - the site was once called Munigiri, 'Abode of Thousand Sages' - and that Lord Sri Rama and Goddess Sita visited and worshipped here during their exile, giving the deity his name. Historical records associate the temple with the Kakatiya, Chalukya, Reddy and Vijayanagara dynasties. In 1983 the temple was renovated under the leadership of Sri Dhanekula Sivannarayana Garu and consecrated by Sri Bharathi Tirtha Swamy; subsequent expansion added a Rajagopuram, a Yagna Mandapam and sub-shrines, and the sacred Nagendra Swamy anthill was restored and reconsecrated in 2013. Local legend also speaks of Nagakanyas (celestial serpent maidens) worshipping the deity at night through the anthill.

name: Sri Ramalingeswara Swamy Vari Devasthanam
town_description: Vijayawada, on the banks of the River Krishna in Andhra Pradesh, is the state's commercial capital and a major pilgrimage hub. It is dominated by the Indrakeeladri hilltop Kanaka Durga Temple, with the Prakasam Barrage and Bhavani Island as other landmarks, and serves as the gateway to Amaravati and the Krishna delta region.

travel.airport: Vijayawada International Airport at Gannavaram (approx. 20 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Vijayawada Railway Station (approx. 6 km), one of South India's busiest junctions.
travel.road: On Yanamalakuduru Konda Road, Yanamalakuduru, southeast Vijayawada (approx. 5-6 km from the city centre). Reachable by steps or motorable cement roads from the north and south sides of the hill; city buses, autos and taxis ply the route.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Maha Shivaratri (February-March) is the grandest and most vibrant time, with Brahmotsavams and Prabha Mahotsavam; Karthika masam (October-November) is also popular. Early mornings and weekdays are best for peaceful darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 6:00 AM to 12:00 noon; evening 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM (verify - the temple's own site lists 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM daily). Special rituals and decorations every Monday and on festive occasions; heavily crowded during Shivaratri and Karthika masam.
